results.note: Every factual claim reproduced; only the severity label is adjusted. Fresh Playwright contexts, no interaction, at 1440x900 and 390x844 (DPR 3, mobile UA): the S3 embed video (section.is-heroheader .hero-bg.w-embed video, no poster, no preload attribute, autoplay muted loop playsinline) fetched Range bytes=0- and received 'bytes 0-6766235/6766236' before any scroll on both viewports (6,608 KiB transferred, readyState 4, buffered 0 to 17.69 s, videoWidth 1440x1078). curl -I on the S3 URL: HTTP/1.1, Content-Length 6766236, Accept-Ranges bytes, no Cache-Control, no Content-Encoding. The second element .hero-bg.hide.w-background-video has computed display:none (live CSS has `.hide{display:none}`) yet its Webflow MP4 (Content-Length 1553967) was also downloaded in full (bytes 0-1553966) on both viewports; the webm variant exists at 5,329,657 bytes and the poster JPG at 20,961 bytes. Page totals: 52 requests / 9,924 KiB before scroll, 58 / 10,350 KiB after scroll, Media 8,126 KiB, identical on desktop and mobile. Lighthouse JSON (not re-run): LCP node is the hero video on home-mobile (5.8 s; TTFB 433, load delay 477, load duration 684 ms) and home-desktop (2.0 s); cache-insight 'Est savings of 8,132 KiB'; total-byte-weight 9,793 / 9,874 KiB; performance 66 mobile. Screenshot shots/verify-5/home-mobile-noscroll.png shows the panther frame as the hero. Severity: the brief's rubric reserves critical for broken, legal or compliance risk, or conversion-blocking issues; this is the largest performance defect on the site but the page works, so it is high (top of the high tier), not critical.

Reproduced. Desktop 1440x900: 38 requests, 13,534 KiB (Lighthouse 13,390 KiB); page footer code runs fetch("https://roscap.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mapwithireee.svg") and the response is 6,659,741 bytes, HTTP/1.1, no Content-Encoding, no Cache-Control (curl -I confirms). I downloaded the SVG: 274 <path>, 53 <text>, 0 <image>/<polygon>, viewBox 0 0 1389 606, 841,128 numeric tokens, 695,704 of them at 3 decimals; rounding every float to 1 decimal gives 4,846,388 bytes (gzip -9: 1,189,300), matching the auditor's 4.8 MB / 1.2 MB claim exactly; gzip of the original is 2,093,699 bytes, so simply serving it compressed would save 4.4 MB. The SVG is not fetched on mobile (mobile shows img.map-mobile mapp-p-1600.png, 135 KiB); DOM 1,328 elements desktop vs 772 mobile. Deal cards: the HTML has 22 img.image elements (22 distinct PNGs) inside .st-thumbnail-wrap, each with srcset offering only a -p-500 variant and the full file (e.g. mayfair-p-500.png 500w, mayfair.png 765w); 10 were fetched in the slider on load: mayfair 1,047,471 B, rome 873,729, manchester 712,908, birminghha 650,567, ssssshefield 639,180, cannes 578,596, dublin 558,739, buckinghamshire 537,600, bathuk 501,723, plus Mask group (1) (204 KiB -p-800 on desktop, 854 KiB full on mobile), rendered at 614x380 CSS px on desktop and 338x380 on the 390 px DPR-3 phone where the full PNG is chosen. Image bytes 6,409 KiB desktop / 7,194 KiB mobile (Lighthouse mobile images 6,386 KiB, image-delivery savings 6,002 KiB; mobile total 7,815 KiB vs LH 7,001). Minor: the auditor's '12 PNGs' is a count of the visible slide set; 22 PNG assets exist and 10 loaded in my run, but the 6 MB figure holds. tr-hero.webp is 130,450 bytes. Severity high is fair for a performance-only issue.

A privacy-policy page is 584 KiB of which 428 KiB is script. Lighthouse mobile: TBT 300 (home), 337 (about), 280 (services), 384 (track), 352 (partner), 321 (insights), 334 (contact), 819 and 364 ms (posts); bootup 1.0 to 1.7 s; gtag long tasks on every mobile run (e.g. 455 + 218 ms on blog-structure, 257 + 140 ms partner, 256 + 179 ms track record); unused-javascript gtag 41%, f2efb 61%, swiper 65%; render-blocking FCP savings 740 ms (services) to 2,120 ms (debt-advisory post), with jQuery 1,106 to 1,458 ms, site CSS 803 to 1,162 ms, Swiper CSS 818 to 1,104 ms, f2efb 666 to 1,050 ms. Script bytes exceed image bytes on Our Services (424 vs 66 KiB), Partner Program (461 vs 83) and Contact (435 vs 211). Severity high fair.

Reproduced. Lighthouse contact-us-mobile: performance 67, FCP 2.3 s, LCP 5.9 s, TBT 334 ms; desktop 85 with TBT 218 ms from long tasks of 137, 122 and 114 ms in webflow.schunk.e24cc. Weight 764 KiB: script 435, image 211, font 103 KiB. LCP node div.page-wrapper > div.main-wrapper > section.section > img.hero-bg (class hero-bg is-contact, Vector-2.svg) with loading=lazy; phases TTFB 417, load delay 408, load 105, render 130 ms; lcp-discovery checklist priorityHinted=false, eagerlyLoaded=false. Playwright: 40 requests, 811 KiB at both 1440x900 and 390x844 (auditor 779 KB); Vector-2.svg 203 KiB brotli-compressed, intrinsic 1441x1260, rendered 1440x900 and 390x873. render-blocking 1,060 ms (jQuery 1,124 ms, site CSS 805 ms). network-dependency-tree longest chain 1,168 ms: /contact-us 452 -> @finsweet/attributes@2/attributes.js 836 -> dist/src-A6N4LPNU.js 1,096 -> dist/chunk-UAA7M346.js 1,168 ms. Live DOM at both viewports: <input ... name="Subject" type="tel" id="Subject" required>; the form has redirect="/contact-us-success" and that URL returns 200 with <meta name="robots" content="noindex">. Screenshot shots/verify-5/contact-mobile-noscroll.png shows the form (the tel type is invisible until focus). Note on severity: the tel keypad on iOS has no letter keys, so a required Subject cannot be typed as text on phones (only digits pass validation), which is a real obstacle on the Ads landing page; high is fair for the composite finding and the Subject item should be treated as the first fix.

Facts reproduced exactly, severity lowered. Parsed the <head> of all 25 sitemap URLs (fresh curl): og:image and twitter:image are absent on every page; og:url, og:site_name and og:locale absent on every page; the 13 static pages carry og:title, og:description, og:type=website, twitter:card=summary_large_image, twitter:title and twitter:description; all 12 /blogs/ posts have zero og:* or twitter:* tags (grep of the full HTML including scripts returns nothing). The consequence 'LinkedIn and WhatsApp previews render without an image' is an inference I could not test (both scrapers may fall back to a page image when og:image is absent). Severity: missing social images do not affect indexing or rankings and only matter when a URL is shared; for a 25-page site with no share buttons this is a polish and brand-consistency issue, not one that clearly hurts trust or conversion for visitors, so medium under the brief's rubric. The recommendation (site-wide default OG image, bind the Blogs template OG fields) stands and is cheap.

Core is real but key details are wrong. I rebuilt the link graph from the fresh HTML of all 25 URLs, excluding <nav>, <header>, <footer>, role=navigation/banner/contentinfo and .navbar/.w-nav/.footer* containers. Correct: /about-us, /partner-program and /insights receive 0 body links; Home's body links are 2 'Explore Our Services' buttons to /our-services and 3 'View Portfolio' buttons to /track-record; /our-services has 1 body link (Get in Touch) and /partner-program 1 (Join The Program), both to /contact-us; /track-record and /contact-us have 0 body links out; the global nav (6 links + CTA) and footer (11 links) give 20 to 21 identical internal links on every page (28 on Home, which carries a second mobile nav); no BreadcrumbList anywhere (0 matches), no related-posts collection list in the post template (post JSON-LD is Article + Organization only); /our-services is self-canonical, has no robots meta, and sitemap.xml lists it with lastmod 2026-08-24T11:48:03Z. Wrong: 'posts contain no links to each other or to /our-services' and 'each post receives exactly 1 [link], from /insights' are false. /blogs/how-real-estate-debt-advisory-works-in-the-uk has 5 in-copy links (to /blogs/roscap-bridging-loan-manchester, /blogs/development-exit-finance, /our-services, /track-record, /contact-us); /blogs/hotel-financing... links 'services' to https://www.roscap.co.uk/our-services; /blogs/uk-buy-to-let-mortgages... links to / and /our-services. So /our-services receives 5 body links from 4 pages (Home x2 and 3 posts), /contact-us receives body links from 3 pages, and 2 posts have 2 inbound body links. 9 of 12 posts have no body links at all. The GSC 'unknown to Google' status is context I cannot verify here. Severity: on a 25-page site where every key page is in the global nav and sitemap, thin contextual linking is a medium SEO priority; the high rating rested on the GSC status and on the overstated 'zero body links'.

Reproduced on 20 fresh Playwright contexts (10 pages x desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844, including two no-interaction, no-scroll runs on / and one on /contact-us). Live HTML of all 25 URLs: <script async src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-H8HS2R6NLS"> and the inline gtag('js') + gtag('config','G-H8HS2R6NLS') both sit before </head> on every page (byte offsets checked); no gtag('consent','default', ...) anywhere. On every capture, with no click or scroll, the browser fetched gtag.js (195 KiB) and fired https://analytics.google.com/g/collect?v=2&tid=G-H8HS2R6NLS&...en=page_view (204) and https://stats.g.doubleclick.net/g/collect?v=2&ngs=1... (204; ngs=1 indicates Google Signals is on). Cookies present after load with no interaction, on every run: _ga and _ga_H8HS2R6NLS on .roscap.co.uk with expiry about 13 months out (expires ~1827971xxx epoch, Dec 2027), plus Cloudflare _cfuvid. No consent UI: a DOM query for [class*=consent], [id*=consent], [class*=cookie], [id*=cookie], [fs-cc], Cookiebot, CookieYes and Osano selectors returned nothing on any page, and the only 'consent' text in the 25 HTML files is policy copy. Aggravating: /cookie-policy states 'Non-essential cookies are used only where you have provided consent via our cookie banner', which is untrue because no banner exists. Performance cost confirmed (gtag long tasks 130 to 455 ms per mobile run, 41% unused). Severity critical is fair: PECR reg 6 consent is required for analytics cookies and the published cookie policy misdescribes the site's behaviour.
